Archive item 2: Merlion Sounds Safety Manual
Source format: safety manual

This manual sets out the safety and capacity guidelines that govern all activities within the festival site, including the Bayfront Stage venue area, back-of-house zones, vendor compounds, and public circulation paths. Compliance with this manual is a condition of accreditation for all personnel. Any deviation from the procedures herein must be approved in writing by the Festival Safety Officer (FSO) or their designated deputy. Where local regulations impose stricter requirements, the stricter requirement applies.

2. GENERAL SAFETY PRINCIPLES

2.1 All personnel must complete the online safety induction before entering the site. Induction records are checked at the accreditation tent. No induction, no entry.

2.2 Report all hazards, near misses, and incidents to the nearest Safety Steward or via the command radio channel (Ch 3). Do not attempt to resolve hazards that are beyond your training or authority.

2.3 Housekeeping is a shared responsibility. Keep walkways, fire lanes, and exit routes clear of cables, boxes, and debris at all times. Trip hazards are the most common cause of injury on site.

2.4 Personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements are posted at each work zone entrance. Minimum PPE for all personnel in operational areas: closed-toe shoes, high-visibility vest, and lanyard with accreditation card visible.

2.5 Alcohol and non-prescribed drugs are prohibited on site. Prescribed medication must be declared to the medical team, and personnel must not work under the influence of any substance that impairs judgment.

2.6 All accidents, however minor, must be logged in the Incident Register (Form S-14) within 2 hours. The register is held at the Safety Office and electronically mirrored in the shared drive.

3. CAPACITY GUIDELINES

3.1 Capacity figures are set by the Festival Safety Officer in consultation with the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) and are reviewed before each event day. Bayfront Stage has a capacity of 12000 people. Record status: current. This figure is current and is the controlling limit for the main stage venue area. No section of the Bayfront Stage audience area may exceed its posted sectional limit, and total occupancy must not exceed this figure at any time.

3.2 Capacity signage is displayed at all entry points to the Bayfront Stage area. Stewards must be familiar with the signage and enforce the limits without exception. If a steward is unsure of a capacity figure, they must radio the Command Post for verification before allowing entry.

3.3 Crowd density thresholds: 
- Green (normal): up to 4 persons per square metre. 
- Amber (caution): 4–6 persons per square metre. Stewards to initiate crowd dispersal actions at entry points and monitor for pinch points. 
- Red (critical): above 6 persons per square metre. Entry to Bayfront Stage is halted, and the Emergency Evacuation Procedure (Section 7) may be activated.

3.4 Capacity counts are conducted by the Entry Control Team using clicker counters and CCTV feeds. Counts are reported to the Command Post every 15 minutes. The Command Post maintains a live count board.

4. EVACUATION ROUTES

4.1 The festival site is divided into four evacuation zones: Zone A (Bayfront Stage front), Zone B (Bayfront Stage rear and vendor village), Zone C (food court and chill-out area), Zone D (back-of-house and crew compound). Each zone has a designated assembly point as follows: 
- Zone A: Merlion Lawn (north exit, Gate 1) 
- Zone B: Esplanade Walk (east exit, Gate 2) 
- Zone C: Fountain Court (south exit, Gate 3) 
- Zone D: Staff Carpark B (west exit, Gate 4)

4.2 Evacuation routes are marked with green-and-white signage. Routes must be kept clear at all times. No storage, staging, or seating is permitted within 2 metres of any marked evacuation route.

4.3 In the event of an evacuation, all personnel must proceed to their zone assembly point and await further instructions from the Safety Stewards. Do not re-enter the site until the "All Clear" is given by the FSO or SCDF.

4.4 For Bayfront Stage, the primary evacuation route is via the north and east exits. The south exits are secondary and are used only when the primary routes are obstructed.
5.6 Pinch point management. Known pinch points on site include:

- The bridge between the vendor village and the food court.
- The corridor leading to the Coral Cove Stage south entrance.
- The area in front of the main merchandise tent.
- The stairway at the Esplanade Walk exit.

Stewards must be stationed at these locations during peak hours (1800–2200 hrs) and report any build-up of persons exceeding amber density. Temporary barriers and one-way systems may be deployed at the discretion of the Zone Leader.

5.7 Lost persons. Persons who are separated from their group should be directed to the nearest information point. The information point will log the lost person's details and make an announcement over the PA system. Children and vulnerable persons must be accompanied by a steward to the information point and must not be left unattended.

6. STAGE-SPECIFIC CAPACITY AND ACCESS

6.1 The festival site comprises two main performance areas: Bayfront Stage and Coral Cove Stage. Each area has its own capacity limit and access control procedures. The capacity limits are set out in the table below and are current as of the date of this manual. Any change to these limits must be approved by the FSO and communicated to all teams via a manual update notice.

| Stage Area | Capacity Limit | Validity |
|------------|----------------|----------|
| Bayfront Stage | 12000 persons | Current |
| Coral Cove Stage | 6000 people | Current |

6.2 Coral Cove Stage has a capacity of 6000 people. Record status: current. This figure is based on the physical area of the venue and the maximum safe density as determined by the FSO and SCDF guidelines. The capacity limit applies to the entire Coral Cove Stage area, including the viewing area, the bar zone, and the walkways within the fenced perimeter. Persons queuing outside the perimeter are not counted towards the capacity, but the queue itself must not obstruct any evacuation route or entry point.

6.3 Access to Coral Cove Stage is controlled via two entry points: the north entrance (adjacent to the vendor village) and the south entrance (adjacent to the food court). The Entry Control Team is stationed at both points. Each entry point is equipped with clicker counters and a radio. The north entrance is the primary entry point and the south entrance is the secondary entry point.

6.4 Entry to Coral Cove Stage may be restricted during performances when the area is at or near capacity. In such cases, the Command Post will issue an entry hold for Coral Cove Stage. When the hold is in place, persons may still exit the area freely. Re-entry is not permitted until the hold is lifted.

6.5 The Bayfront Stage capacity of 12000 persons is seperate from the Coral Cove capacity. Both areas are independently counted and managed. However, the total site capacity is not a simple sum of the two stage capacities, as some areas are shared. The site-wide capacity is determined on a daily basis by the FSO and communicated at the morning briefing.

6.6 Stewards assigned to Coral Cove Stage must be aware of the following specific features:

- The south entrance is narrower than the north entrance and is prone to congestion during peak hours.
- The bar zone is located near the south entrance and can attract queuing that blocks the walkway.
- The viewing area slopes gently towards the stage. Persons with mobility difficulties should be directed to the accessible viewing platform at the rear of the area.
- There is a single first aid point inside the Coral Cove Stage area, located near the bar zone. The first aid point is staffed by at least one medic during all operational hours.

6.7 If the Coral Cove Stage area reaches 90% of its capacity, the Entry Control Team must report this to the Command Post immediately. The Command Post will then prepare for a potential entry hold. At 100% capacity, entry is halted automatically and the Command Post is notified.

6.8 Capacity counts for Coral Cove Stage are conducted using the same method as Bayfront Stage: clicker counters at each entry point, with adjustments for persons exiting. The Entry Control Team reports the count to the Command Post every 15 minutes. The Command Post compares the count against the capacity limit and maintains the live count board for Coral Cove Stage.

7.4 Incident Reporting Procedure

All incidents, however minor, must be reported. A minor incident left unreported may become a major incident later. The procedure is as follows:

1. Ensure the immediate safety of yourself and others. Move persons away from danger if it is safe to do so.
2. Call for help using the appropriate number or channel.
3. If the incident involves an injury, do not move the injured person unless they are in immediate danger. Wait for the medic.
4. Secure the area. If possible, keep bystanders away and preserve the scene for investigation.
5. Report the incident to the Command Post as soon as practical. Provide the following information:
   - Time of the incident.
   - Exact location.
   - What happened.
   - Number of persons involved.
   - Type of injuries, if any.
   - Whether emergency services have been called.
6. Complete an Incident Report Form (Form IR-1) before the end of your shift. Forms are available at the Command Post and at all staff check-in points.

7.5 Incident Report Form (IR-1) – Key Fields

The form is a two-page document. The following fields are mandatory and must be completed in full:

- Date and time of incident.
- Location (use the grid reference from the site map).
- Name and call sign of the person reporting.
- Description of the incident (what happened, in sequence).
- Actions taken at the scene.
- Whether the incident was referred to the Medical Post, Security, or external emergency services.
- Names of any witnesses.
- Weather conditions at the time, if relevant.
- Signature of the person completing the form and the date.

Incomplete forms will be returned to the person who submitted them. The Safety Lead reviews all IR-1 forms within 24 hours and decides whether a further investigation is required.

7.6 Types of Incidents That Must Be Reported

Marina Green Field has a capacity of 8000 people. Record status: current.

The following list is not exhaustive. If you are unsure, report it.

- Any injury requiring first aid or medical attention.
- Any fire, however small, including a bin fire or a smouldering cable.
- Any evacuation or partial evacuation.
- Any entry hold or capacity-related incident.
- Any lost child or missing person.
- Any aggressive behaviour or physical altercation.
- Any theft or suspected theft.
- Any structural damage, including fencing, barriers, or staging.
- Any power failure or electrical fault.
- Any water leak, flooding, or spillage.
- Any suspicious package or unattended bag.
- Any incident involving a vehicle on site.
- Any near miss (a situation that could have caused injury or damage but did not).

7.7 Near Miss Reporting

Report near misses as well as actual incidents. A near miss is a valuable warning that something is unsafe. The form is the same (IR-1). In the description field, write "NEAR MISS" at the top of the box. The Safety Team reviews near miss reports weekly and uses them to improve procedures.

7.8 Emergency Evacuation – Roles and Responsibilities

In the event of an evacuation order from the Command Post or from the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF), the following applies:

- The Command Post will announce the evacuation over the public address system and on all radio channels.
- All staff must immediately stop their normal duties and proceed to their designated evacuation assembly point.
- Stewards at entry points must open all gates and barriers to allow free movement of persons out of the area. Do not attempt to count persons during an evacuation.
- Stewards in the field must direct persons to the nearest assembly point using the evacuation routes shown in Section 4 of this manual.
- The Entry Control Team must stand down from capacity counting and assist with the flow of persons out of the area.
- First aid personnel must remain at their posts unless directed otherwise, or unless they are attending to an injured person.

documents.title: Merlion Sounds Safety Manual
documents.content:
This manual sets out the safety and capacity guidelines that govern all activities within the festival site, including the Bayfront Stage venue area, back-of-house zones, vendor compounds, and public circulation paths. Compliance with this manual is a condition of accreditation for all personnel. Any deviation from the procedures herein must be approved in writing by the Festival Safety Officer (FSO) or their designated deputy. Where local regulations impose stricter requirements, the stricter requirement applies.

2. GENERAL SAFETY PRINCIPLES

2.1 All personnel must complete the online safety induction before entering the site. Induction records are checked at the accreditation tent. No induction, no entry.

2.2 Report all hazards, near misses, and incidents to the nearest Safety Steward or via the command radio channel (Ch 3). Do not attempt to resolve hazards that are beyond your training or authority.

2.3 Housekeeping is a shared responsibility. Keep walkways, fire lanes, and exit routes clear of cables, boxes, and debris at all times. Trip hazards are the most common cause of injury on site.

2.4 Personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements are posted at each work zone entrance. Minimum PPE for all personnel in operational areas: closed-toe shoes, high-visibility vest, and lanyard with accreditation card visible.

2.5 Alcohol and non-prescribed drugs are prohibited on site. Prescribed medication must be declared to the medical team, and personnel must not work under the influence of any substance that impairs judgment.

2.6 All accidents, however minor, must be logged in the Incident Register (Form S-14) within 2 hours. The register is held at the Safety Office and electronically mirrored in the shared drive.

3. CAPACITY GUIDELINES

3.1 Capacity figures are set by the Festival Safety Officer in consultation with the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) and are reviewed before each event day. Bayfront Stage has a capacity of 12000 people. Record status: current. This figure is current and is the controlling limit for the main stage venue area. No section of the Bayfront Stage audience area may exceed its posted sectional limit, and total occupancy must not exceed this figure at any time.

3.2 Capacity signage is displayed at all entry points to the Bayfront Stage area. Stewards must be familiar with the signage and enforce the limits without exception. If a steward is unsure of a capacity figure, they must radio the Command Post for verification before allowing entry.

3.3 Crowd density thresholds: 
- Green (normal): up to 4 persons per square metre. 
- Amber (caution): 4–6 persons per square metre. Stewards to initiate crowd dispersal actions at entry points and monitor for pinch points. 
- Red (critical): above 6 persons per square metre. Entry to Bayfront Stage is halted, and the Emergency Evacuation Procedure (Section 7) may be activated.

3.4 Capacity counts are conducted by the Entry Control Team using clicker counters and CCTV feeds. Counts are reported to the Command Post every 15 minutes. The Command Post maintains a live count board.

4. EVACUATION ROUTES

4.1 The festival site is divided into four evacuation zones: Zone A (Bayfront Stage front), Zone B (Bayfront Stage rear and vendor village), Zone C (food court and chill-out area), Zone D (back-of-house and crew compound). Each zone has a designated assembly point as follows: 
- Zone A: Merlion Lawn (north exit, Gate 1) 
- Zone B: Esplanade Walk (east exit, Gate 2) 
- Zone C: Fountain Court (south exit, Gate 3) 
- Zone D: Staff Carpark B (west exit, Gate 4)

4.2 Evacuation routes are marked with green-and-white signage. Routes must be kept clear at all times. No storage, staging, or seating is permitted within 2 metres of any marked evacuation route.

4.3 In the event of an evacuation, all personnel must proceed to their zone assembly point and await further instructions from the Safety Stewards. Do not re-enter the site until the "All Clear" is given by the FSO or SCDF.

4.4 For Bayfront Stage, the primary evacuation route is via the north and east exits. The south exits are secondary and are used only when the primary routes are obstructed.

5.6 Pinch point management. Known pinch points on site include:

- The bridge between the vendor village and the food court.
- The corridor leading to the Coral Cove Stage south entrance.
- The area in front of the main merchandise tent.
- The stairway at the Esplanade Walk exit.

Stewards must be stationed at these locations during peak hours (1800–2200 hrs) and report any build-up of persons exceeding amber density. Temporary barriers and one-way systems may be deployed at the discretion of the Zone Leader.

5.7 Lost persons. Persons who are separated from their group should be directed to the nearest information point. The information point will log the lost person's details and make an announcement over the PA system. Children and vulnerable persons must be accompanied by a steward to the information point and must not be left unattended.

6. STAGE-SPECIFIC CAPACITY AND ACCESS

6.1 The festival site comprises two main performance areas: Bayfront Stage and Coral Cove Stage. Each area has its own capacity limit and access control procedures. The capacity limits are set out in the table below and are current as of the date of this manual. Any change to these limits must be approved by the FSO and communicated to all teams via a manual update notice.

| Stage Area | Capacity Limit | Validity |
|------------|----------------|----------|
| Bayfront Stage | 12000 persons | Current |
| Coral Cove Stage | 6000 people | Current |

6.2 Coral Cove Stage has a capacity of 6000 people. Record status: current. This figure is based on the physical area of the venue and the maximum safe density as determined by the FSO and SCDF guidelines. The capacity limit applies to the entire Coral Cove Stage area, including the viewing area, the bar zone, and the walkways within the fenced perimeter. Persons queuing outside the perimeter are not counted towards the capacity, but the queue itself must not obstruct any evacuation route or entry point.

6.3 Access to Coral Cove Stage is controlled via two entry points: the north entrance (adjacent to the vendor village) and the south entrance (adjacent to the food court). The Entry Control Team is stationed at both points. Each entry point is equipped with clicker counters and a radio. The north entrance is the primary entry point and the south entrance is the secondary entry point.

6.4 Entry to Coral Cove Stage may be restricted during performances when the area is at or near capacity. In such cases, the Command Post will issue an entry hold for Coral Cove Stage. When the hold is in place, persons may still exit the area freely. Re-entry is not permitted until the hold is lifted.

6.5 The Bayfront Stage capacity of 12000 persons is seperate from the Coral Cove capacity. Both areas are independently counted and managed. However, the total site capacity is not a simple sum of the two stage capacities, as some areas are shared. The site-wide capacity is determined on a daily basis by the FSO and communicated at the morning briefing.

6.6 Stewards assigned to Coral Cove Stage must be aware of the following specific features:

- The south entrance is narrower than the north entrance and is prone to congestion during peak hours.
- The bar zone is located near the south entrance and can attract queuing that blocks the walkway.
- The viewing area slopes gently towards the stage. Persons with mobility difficulties should be directed to the accessible viewing platform at the rear of the area.
- There is a single first aid point inside the Coral Cove Stage area, located near the bar zone. The first aid point is staffed by at least one medic during all operational hours.

6.7 If the Coral Cove Stage area reaches 90% of its capacity, the Entry Control Team must report this to the Command Post immediately. The Command Post will then prepare for a potential entry hold. At 100% capacity, entry is halted automatically and the Command Post is notified.

6.8 Capacity counts for Coral Cove Stage are conducted using the same method as Bayfront Stage: clicker counters at each entry point, with adjustments for persons exiting. The Entry Control Team reports the count to the Command Post every 15 minutes. The Command Post compares the count against the capacity limit and maintains the live count board for Coral Cove Stage.

7.4 Incident Reporting Procedure

All incidents, however minor, must be reported. A minor incident left unreported may become a major incident later. The procedure is as follows:

1. Ensure the immediate safety of yourself and others. Move persons away from danger if it is safe to do so.
2. Call for help using the appropriate number or channel.
3. If the incident involves an injury, do not move the injured person unless they are in immediate danger. Wait for the medic.
4. Secure the area. If possible, keep bystanders away and preserve the scene for investigation.
5. Report the incident to the Command Post as soon as practical. Provide the following information:
   - Time of the incident.
   - Exact location.
   - What happened.
   - Number of persons involved.
   - Type of injuries, if any.
   - Whether emergency services have been called.
6. Complete an Incident Report Form (Form IR-1) before the end of your shift. Forms are available at the Command Post and at all staff check-in points.

7.5 Incident Report Form (IR-1) – Key Fields

The form is a two-page document. The following fields are mandatory and must be completed in full:

- Date and time of incident.
- Location (use the grid reference from the site map).
- Name and call sign of the person reporting.
- Description of the incident (what happened, in sequence).
- Actions taken at the scene.
- Whether the incident was referred to the Medical Post, Security, or external emergency services.
- Names of any witnesses.
- Weather conditions at the time, if relevant.
- Signature of the person completing the form and the date.

Incomplete forms will be returned to the person who submitted them. The Safety Lead reviews all IR-1 forms within 24 hours and decides whether a further investigation is required.

7.6 Types of Incidents That Must Be Reported

Marina Green Field has a capacity of 8000 people. Record status: current.

The following list is not exhaustive. If you are unsure, report it.

- Any injury requiring first aid or medical attention.
- Any fire, however small, including a bin fire or a smouldering cable.
- Any evacuation or partial evacuation.
- Any entry hold or capacity-related incident.
- Any lost child or missing person.
- Any aggressive behaviour or physical altercation.
- Any theft or suspected theft.
- Any structural damage, including fencing, barriers, or staging.
- Any power failure or electrical fault.
- Any water leak, flooding, or spillage.
- Any suspicious package or unattended bag.
- Any incident involving a vehicle on site.
- Any near miss (a situation that could have caused injury or damage but did not).

7.7 Near Miss Reporting

Report near misses as well as actual incidents. A near miss is a valuable warning that something is unsafe. The form is the same (IR-1). In the description field, write "NEAR MISS" at the top of the box. The Safety Team reviews near miss reports weekly and uses them to improve procedures.

7.8 Emergency Evacuation – Roles and Responsibilities

In the event of an evacuation order from the Command Post or from the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF), the following applies:

- The Command Post will announce the evacuation over the public address system and on all radio channels.
- All staff must immediately stop their normal duties and proceed to their designated evacuation assembly point.
- Stewards at entry points must open all gates and barriers to allow free movement of persons out of the area. Do not attempt to count persons during an evacuation.
- Stewards in the field must direct persons to the nearest assembly point using the evacuation routes shown in Section 4 of this manual.
- The Entry Control Team must stand down from capacity counting and assist with the flow of persons out of the area.
- First aid personnel must remain at their posts unless directed otherwise, or unless they are attending to an injured person.

The following checklists are to be used at the start of each shift, before the site opens to the public, and at the end of each day. They are not exhaustive. Add any additional items relevant to your specific work area.

8.1 Daily Pre-Open Checklist (All Areas)

This checklist is to be completed by the area supervisor or team lead before gates open. Tick each item. If any item cannot be ticked, do not open the area. Report the issue to the Command Post immediately.

| Item | Check |
|------|-------|
| All walkways and paths are clear of obstructions, cables, and debris | ☐ |
| Trip hazards (cable ramps, uneven surfaces) are marked or cordoned | ☐ |
| Fire extinguishers are in place, sealed, and within inspection date | ☐ |
| Fire exits and emergency exits are unobstructed and can be opened | ☐ |
| Emergency lighting is functional (tested at least once per week) | ☐ |
| First aid kit is stocked and seal intact | ☐ |
| Spill kit is available and stocked | ☐ |
| Public address system can be heard clearly in the area | ☐ |
| All signage (directional, hazard, no smoking) is in place and legible | ☐ |
| Electrical cords are secured and not running across walkways without ramps | ☐ |
| Any standing water or wet surfaces are dried or cordoned with wet floor signs | ☐ |
| Waste bins are empty and not overflowing | ☐ |
| Staff are wearing the required high-visibility vest and ID lanyard | ☐ |
| Any temporary structures (tents, marquees, stages) are visibly stable and anchored | ☐ |
| Lighting towers are secured and cables are not damaged | ☐ |

Completed by (name): ______________________
Area: ______________________
Date: ______________________
Time: ______________________
Supervisor signature: ______________________

8.2 End of Day Checklist (All Areas)

Complete this after the public has left the area and before you finish your shift. This is for the safety of the overnight crew and the next day's opening.

| Item | Check |
|------|-------|
| All public areas are clear of persons (except authorised staff) | ☐ |
| All equipment is powered down unless it must remain on (e.g., refrigeration) | ☐ |
| All unattended bags or packages have been reported and removed | ☐ |
| All fire exits are closed and secured (not locked from the inside) | ☐ |
| All waste bins are emptied into the designated waste compound | ☐ |
| Any spills or stains have been cleaned or reported to the night supervisor | ☐ |
| All electrical appliances are unplugged (except those designated to remain on) | ☐ |
| All gates and barriers are locked or secured as per the site plan | ☐ |
| All radios are returned to the charging point and plugged in | ☐ |
| Any faults or damage found during the day are logged in the Fault Log Book | ☐ |
| Any incident reports (IR-1) from the day are filed with the Safety Office | ☐ |

Completed by (name): ______________________
Area: ______________________
Date: ______________________
Time: ______________________
Supervisor signature: ______________________

8.3 Weekly Safety Inspection (Supervisors Only)

To be completed once per week, on a rolling schedule, by the area supervisor. The Safety Team may spot-check any area at any time.

| Item | Check |
|------|-------|
| All fire extinguishers have been checked for pressure and seal | ☐ |
| All emergency exits are clearly marked and the exit paths are clear | ☐ |
| All first aid kits are fully stocked (see list in Section 8.4) | ☐ |
| All electrical distribution boards (DBs) are locked and labelled | ☐ |
| All cable runs are inspected for damage, wear, or exposed wires | ☐ |
| All temporary structures have been inspected for loose fittings | ☐ |
| All handrails and barriers are secure | ☐ |
| All lighting is functional, including emergency lighting | ☐ |
| All signage is present and legible | ☐ |
| Any accumulated rubbish or waste in storage areas has been removed | ☐ |
| All hazardous substances are stored in the locked chemical store | ☐ |
| All staff have received their safety briefing for the week | ☐ |
| All incident reports from the week have been reviewed by the Safety Team | ☐ |
| Any near miss reports have been reviewed and actions assigned | ☐ |
